content: You are a knowledge extraction system for AI-assisted workflow audits. You identify learnings from session event logs: corrections (human caught an AI mistake), gotchas (surprising findings), decisions (important rejected/revised choices), prompt_pattern (prompt strategies that were especially effective or ineffective — e.g., accuracy improvements from prompt changes, failed prompting approaches, effective few-shot patterns), and general learnings. When session events reveal a decision chain about prompt refinement (revisions mentioning prompts, accuracy changes, or strategy shifts), extract a prompt_pattern learning noting what worked, what didn't, and why. Be selective — only extract insights that would help in future sessions. Do NOT duplicate existing learnings.

Session ID: trace_20260101_abc123
Project: collab-a

Events:
[evt_001] type=annotation | actor=ai | category=gotcha | content="The cache key ignores the locale." | tags=['cache']
[evt_002] type=decision | description="Key the cache by locale as well as path." | disposition=proposed | proposed_by=ai | rationale="Two locales served each other's pages."
[evt_003] type=contribution | description="Added a locale-aware cache key." | direction=human | execution=ai | artifact=cache.py

Existing learnings (DO NOT duplicate):
- [lrn_001] (decision) "Retry the upload at most three times."
- [lrn_002] (gotcha) "The staging bucket is read-only."

Extract NEW learnings from these events. For each learning:
- "content": a specific account of what was learned (1-3 sentences)
- "category": one of learning, correction, gotcha, decision, observation, prompt_pattern
- "tags": 2-5 relevant tags for future retrieval
- "source_event": the event ID this learning primarily comes from
- "corrects_event_ids": list of event IDs being corrected (for corrections only)

Return a JSON object with key "learnings" containing an array of objects.
If no new learnings exist, return {"learnings": []}.

Keep each learning within the scope of its source event: say what happened and where (in this session and project, what was found, decided, corrected or built), and do not widen it into a rule for other work. Word a learning as a general rule or instruction only when its source is a decision with disposition "accepted" and resolved_by=human that states that rule itself. A rule, instruction or judgement from any other source (an AI's note, a decision an AI resolved or nobody resolved) is reported as that source's claim, for example "An AI note in this session held that ...", never as a rule. Facts that were found or measured are stated plainly.

A decision whose disposition is "proposed" has not been accepted by anyone. If a learning's source_event is such a decision, word the learning as a proposal (for example "It was proposed that ..."), never as a rule or an instruction.
